name: Revelation
sourceNote: This translation was made directly from the Greek text of Westcott and Hort (1881; public domain), published under the title *The New Testament in the Original Greek*, with Tischendorf’s eighth edition (1869–72; public domain) consulted. It is not made from any other Greek edition. The SBL Greek New Testament, the Nestle–Aland *Novum Testamentum Graece*, and the Robinson–Pierpont Byzantine text were consulted only to see where their readings differ, so that variants could be noted; no wording from them is reproduced. The English was written afresh from the Greek and checked against modern translations so that their wording is not reproduced either. Where manuscript readings are cited in the notes, they are reported from the standard editions and have not been verified against the manuscripts. Greek *kyrios* is rendered “Lord”; where an Old Testament passage with the divine name is quoted or echoed, a note gives the Hebrew *Yahweh*. *Christos* is rendered “Christ” where it functions as part of Jesus’ name. The writer names himself John (1:1, 4, 9; 22:8), a prophet exiled on the island of Patmos. From the 2nd century (Justin, Irenaeus) many identified him with John the apostle, while Dionysius of Alexandria (3rd century) argued from its Greek style that the author was a different John; this translation takes no position. Irenaeus dates the visions near the end of the reign of Domitian (about AD 95); some scholars prefer the late 60s. The Greek of Revelation is often unusual in grammar, and this translation does not smooth it entirely. The chief early witnesses include the papyri P18, P24, P47 (3rd century), P98 and P115 (3rd–4th century), Codex Sinaiticus, Codex Alexandrinus (often judged the best witness for this book) and Codex Ephraemi; Codex Vaticanus lacks Revelation. Erasmus’s first printed Greek text (1516), the basis of the King James Version, rested on one incomplete 12th-century manuscript, and he supplied the last six verses by translating from Latin. Measures are given in modern equivalents, with the original units in the notes. Hymns and songs are set as poetry.

verses.text: The unveiling of Jesus Christ, which God gave him in order to show his slaves what must happen before long. Jesus signified it by dispatching his angel to his slave John,{a}
He has testified to God’s word and to what Jesus Christ attested, all that he saw.
Blessed is the person who reads this prophecy aloud, and blessed are the ones who listen to it and hold fast to the things written here, because the appointed time is close.{b}
John, to the seven churches in Asia: favor and peace to you from him who is, and was, and is on his way, and from the seven spirits that stand before his throne,{c}
and from Jesus Christ, the witness who keeps faith, first of the dead to be born to life, ruler over earth’s kings. ¶To him who loves us, who by his own blood has freed us from our sins,{d}
and made us a royal house, priests for God, his Father. To him belong glory and dominion through the ages of ages. Amen.{e}

Behold, he comes among the clouds,
and every eye will look on him,
even the ones who stabbed him,
and all the peoples of the land will beat their breasts for him.
Yes, truly. Amen.{f}
“I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, who is, and was, and is on his way, the Almighty.{g}

I am John, your brother and your companion in the tribulation, the kingdom, and the perseverance that belong to Jesus. I came to be on the island named Patmos on account of God’s word and the witness of Jesus.{h}
In the Spirit I came to be, on the Lord’s day, and behind me I heard a great voice, resounding like a trumpet,{i}
and it said, “Whatever you see, write it in a scroll and transmit it to the seven churches—Ephesus and Smyrna and Pergamum and Thyatira and Sardis and Philadelphia and Laodicea.”{j}
So I wheeled around to look at the voice that was speaking to me. On wheeling, I observed seven lampstands made of gold,
and in the midst of the lampstands a figure like a son of man, wearing a garment that reached to his feet and a golden band across his breast.{k}
His head and hair shone with a whiteness like wool or fresh snow, and his eyes blazed like fire;{l}
his feet resembled bronze glowing hot in a kiln, and his voice rang out like a roar of many waters.{m}
His right hand held seven stars. A sharp sword with two edges projected from his mouth. His face shone as the sun does at midday.
On seeing him, I fell at his feet like one who was dead. Then he rested his right hand upon me, saying, “Fear not. I am the first and the last,{n}
as well as the one who lives. I died, and see, I am alive for all the ages, and I hold the keys of Death and of Hades.{o}
So write what you have seen, both what is now and what is to happen after this.

This is the secret of the seven stars that you saw at my right hand, and of the seven golden lampstands: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches themselves.{p}

notes.text: Revelation: Greek *apokalypsis*, “unveiling.” *Jesus*: Greek form of the Hebrew *Yeshuaʿ*, “Yahweh saves.” *John*: from the Hebrew *Yoḥanan*, “Yahweh is gracious.” *Slaves*: Greek *douloi*, “slaves,” “servants.”
Happy: or “blessed”; so in the other six beatitudes of the book (22:14, 22:7, 20:6, 19:9, 16:15 and 14:13). *Reads aloud*: that is, in the assembly.

Asia: the Roman province in the west of what is now Turkey. *The one who is*: compare Exod 3:14 in the Greek Old Testament, where God names himself. *Seven spirits*: perhaps the Holy Spirit in his fullness (compare Isa 11:2; Zech 4:2–10), or seven angelic beings.
Ps 89:27, 37 (Greek Old Testament 88:28, 38). *Set us free*: later manuscripts read “washed.” *Our sins*: Westcott and Hort bracket “our.”
Exod 19:6. *Forever and ever*: literally “to the ages of the ages”; so throughout.

Alpha … Omega: the opening and closing letters of the Greek alphabet; compare 21:6; 22:13. Later manuscripts add “the beginning and the end.” *The Lord God … the Almighty*: in the Greek Old Testament *kyrios ho theos ho pantokratōr* renders Hebrew *Yahweh ʾElohe tsevaʾot*, “Yahweh, God of Armies” (for example Amos 3:13; 4:13).
Brother: Greek *adelphos*; the plural *adelphoi* in this book includes sisters. *Patmos*: a small Aegean island lying roughly 37 miles (60 km) southwest of Miletus.
In the Spirit: or “in spirit,” that is, in a prophetic trance. *The Lord’s day*: Greek *kyriakē hēmera*, probably Sunday.

The seven cities lie on a circular road in the province of Asia. *Ephesus*: perhaps “desirable.” *Smyrna*: “myrrh.” *Pergamum*: perhaps “citadel.” *Thyatira*: of uncertain meaning. *Sardis*: of uncertain meaning. *Philadelphia*: “brotherly love,” named after King Attalus II Philadelphus. *Laodicea*: “justice of the people,” named after Laodice, a Seleucid queen. Later manuscripts add at the start of the verse “I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last.”
Son of man: compare Dan 7:13; 10:5–6.
Compare Dan 7:9.
Fine bronze: Greek *chalkolibanon*, a word not found before this book, apparently a fine alloy of bronze. Compare Ezek 1:24; 43:2.
Compare Isa 44:6; 48:12.
Hades: the Greek name for the realm of the dead. Later manuscripts add “Amen.”
Angels: or “messengers”; the Greek word *angelos* means both.

verses.text: “To the angel of the church in Ephesus, write: ¶‘These are the words of him who grips the seven stars in his right hand and walks about among the seven golden lampstands:

I know your works—how hard you labor and how you persevere—and that you cannot endure bad people. You tested those who claim to be apostles though they are not, and you discovered that they were liars.
You are enduring, and for my name’s sake you have borne hardships without growing weary.
But I hold this against you, that you have left the love you had at first.

Call to mind, then, the height you fell from; turn back, and act as you did in the beginning. Otherwise I am coming to you, and unless you turn back I will take your lampstand away from where it stands.
But you have this to your credit: you detest what the Nicolaitans do, as I do too.{a}
Anyone who has an ear, let him pay attention to the Spirit’s message for the churches. I will give the conqueror a share of the tree of life, which grows in the paradise of God.’{b}
“To the angel of the Smyrna church write: ¶‘Thus speaks the first and the last, who became dead and came alive again:
I am aware of your tribulation and poverty—yet you are rich—and of the blasphemy against you by people claiming to be Jews who are not, but are Satan’s synagogue.{c}

Do not be afraid of what you will soon suffer. Notice: the devil is going to put some of you in prison as a test, and you will endure tribulation for ten days. Prove faithful to the point of dying, and I will present you with the crown of life.{d}
Anyone who has an ear, let him pay attention to the Spirit’s message for the churches. The one who conquers will suffer no injury from the second death.’
“To the angel of the church in Pergamum, write: ¶‘These are the words of him who holds the sharp, double-edged sword:

I am aware of where you dwell, where Satan’s throne stands. You keep a firm hold on my name, and you never abandoned your faith in me, even during the days when Antipas, my faithful witness, was killed in your midst, where Satan dwells.{e}

But a few matters count against you. There are people with you who maintain the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balak to lay a trap before the people of Israel: to eat idol sacrifices and to fornicate.{f}
In the same way you also have some who adhere to the teaching of the Nicolaitans.
Repent, then. If not, I am coming against you swiftly, and I will fight them with the sword of my mouth.

Anyone who has an ear, let him pay attention to the Spirit’s message for the churches. I will give the conqueror a portion of the concealed manna. I will give him a white pebble as well, and engraved on the pebble is a new name, which nobody recognizes except its recipient.’{g}
“To the angel of the Thyatira church write: ¶‘Thus speaks the Son of God, the one with eyes like a blaze of fire and with feet like burnished bronze:{h}
I am aware of your works—your love, faith, ministry, and perseverance—and that your recent works exceed the earlier ones.
Yet this is my complaint against you: you put up with Jezebel, that woman who declares herself a prophetess; she instructs my slaves and misleads them into fornicating and eating idol sacrifices.{i}
Time to repent was given to her, but she is unwilling to turn back from her fornication.
Watch: I will cast her on a bed, and her fellow adulterers into severe tribulation, if they do not repent of her deeds.{j}
Her children I will strike with death, and every church will come to know that I am he who probes the inner self and the heart, and that I will repay each one of you as your deeds deserve.{k}
But to the remaining ones in Thyatira—as many as lack this teaching, such as have not known the so-called “deep things of Satan”—I tell you: I am not loading any other burden on you;{l}
just keep a firm grip on what you have until I arrive.
To the conqueror, who guards my works right to the end, I will grant authority over the nations,
and he will shepherd them with an iron rod, as clay vessels are smashed to pieces, just as I too have received it from my Father;{m}
and I will hand him the morning star.
Anyone who has an ear, let him pay attention to the Spirit’s message for the churches.’

notes.text: Nicolaitans: a group otherwise known only from later reports; the name may mean “conqueror of the people.” Compare verse 15.
Gen 2:9; 3:22. *Paradise*: a Persian word for a walled garden or park, used in the Greek Old Testament for the garden of Eden.
Satan: Hebrew *satan*, “adversary,” “accuser.” Later manuscripts add “your works” after “I know.”
Devil: Greek *diabolos*, “slanderer.”

Antipas: “in place of the father,” a shortened form of Antipater; nothing more is known of him. *My faithful one*: Westcott and Hort bracket the second “my.” *Satan’s throne*: perhaps the great altar of Zeus, the temple of Augustus, or the city as a center of the imperial cult.
Num 25:1–3; 31:16. *Balaam*: perhaps “devourer.” *Balak*: “devastator.” *Israel*: “God strives” or “he strives with God” (Gen 32:28).
Manna: Exod 16:31–35. *Pebble*: Greek *psēphos*, a small smooth stone. Its meaning here is uncertain; white pebbles were used in antiquity as tokens of acquittal, admission or membership.
Eyes: Westcott and Hort bracket “his” before “eyes.”
Jezebel: the name of King Ahab’s wife (1 Kgs 16:31; 21:25–26; 2 Kgs 9:22), used here of a prophetess in Thyatira; perhaps “where is the prince?” *The woman*: many manuscripts read “your wife.”
Her works: some manuscripts read “their works.”
Strike with death: literally “kill with death,” perhaps “with plague.” *Minds*: literally “kidneys,” regarded as the seat of the feelings. Compare Jer 17:10.
Compare Acts 15:28.
Ps 2:8–9 in the Greek Old Testament. *Shepherd*: or “rule.”

verses.text: “To the angel of the Sardis church write: ¶‘Thus speaks he who possesses the seven spirits of God and the seven stars: I am aware of your works—that you bear a name saying you live, though you are dead.
Wake up! Shore up what is left, for it is on the point of dying. I have not found what you have done to be complete before my God.
Call to mind, therefore, what you received and heard; guard it, and repent. If you do not rouse yourself, I will arrive like a thief, and you will not learn at which hour I will reach you.
Still, there are a few people in Sardis whose clothing is unstained; they will walk at my side dressed in white, for they deserve it.{a}
Thus will the conqueror be clothed in white clothes; and his name I will never blot out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father and before his angels.
Anyone who has an ear, let him pay attention to the Spirit’s message for the churches.’
“To the angel of the Philadelphia church write: ¶‘Thus speaks the holy one, the genuine one, who holds the key of David; what he opens, none will close, and what he closes, none opens:{b}
I am aware of your works. Observe: I have placed before you a doorway, opened, that nobody has power to close. You possess little strength; still, you kept my word and did not deny my name.
Observe, I am handing over some from Satan’s synagogue, who call themselves Jews and are not, but are liars. I will cause them to arrive and kneel at your feet, and to learn that I have loved you.{c}
Since you guarded my message of patient endurance, I in turn will guard you from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the entire inhabited world, to try the people living on earth.
I am coming quickly. Keep a firm grip on what you have, so that nobody robs you of your crown.

The victor I will make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he will go out from it no more. I will write on him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God—the new Jerusalem that comes down out of heaven from my God—and also my own new name.{d}
Anyone who has an ear, let him pay attention to the Spirit’s message for the churches.’
“To the angel of the Laodicea church write: ¶‘Thus speaks the Amen, the reliable and genuine witness, the source of God’s creation:{e}
I am aware of your works, that you are not cold and not hot. I would prefer you to be either cold or hot.
Thus, because you are warm and neither hot nor cold, I intend to spit you out of my mouth.{f}
You keep saying, “I am rich; I have grown wealthy; there is nothing I lack.” You do not realize that it is you who are miserable and pitiful, poor and blind and naked.{g}

I advise you to acquire from me gold fired and purified, to make you wealthy; also white garments for you to wear, so that your disgraceful nudity is concealed; and ointment to put on your eyes, that you may see.{h}
I correct and train everyone I love. Be zealous, then, and change your ways.{i}
Look at me, standing at the door and knocking! Should anyone hear my voice and open the door, I will enter and dine with that person, and he with me.
To the one who prevails I will grant a place beside me on my throne, as I too prevailed and sat down with my Father on his throne.
Anyone who has an ear, let him pay attention to the Spirit’s message for the churches.’”

notes.text: People: literally “names.”
Isa 22:22. *David*: “beloved.”
Jerusalem: perhaps “foundation of peace.”
Amen: a Hebrew word meaning “firm,” “true”; compare Isa 65:16. *Beginning*: or “origin,” “ruler.” *True*: Westcott and Hort bracket the article before this word.
Laodicea’s water was piped in from a distance and arrived tepid, unlike the hot springs of nearby Hierapolis and the cold water of Colossae.
Compare Hos 12:8.
Laodicea was a banking center, known for its black wool and for a medical school associated with an eye remedy.
Compare Prov 3:12.

verses.text: After this I looked, and an open door appeared in heaven. The first voice, the one I had heard like a trumpet speaking with me, now said, “Climb up here, and I will let you see what must occur after these events.”
At once I was in the Spirit. There in heaven stood a throne, with someone seated on the throne.
The one seated there looked like jasper and carnelian in appearance, and around the throne was a rainbow resembling an emerald.{a}
Encircling the throne stood twenty-four other thrones, and on them sat twenty-four elders dressed in white, wearing crowns of gold.
Out of the throne burst lightning, rumbling and thunder, while in front of it seven fiery torches were burning, the seven spirits of God;{b}
and in front of the throne lay what seemed a glass sea like crystal. ¶In the center, around the throne, stood four living beings with eyes covering them, front and back.{c}
The first being resembled a lion, the second a young bull, the third had a human-looking face, and the fourth resembled an eagle in flight.{d}

Each of the four living creatures has six wings and is covered with eyes, round about and underneath, and without rest, by day or by night, they keep saying,
“Holy, holy, holy,
Lord God Almighty,
who was and who is and who is coming!”{e}
Whenever the living beings render glory, honor, and thanks to the occupant of the throne, who lives to the ages of ages,
the twenty-four elders will prostrate themselves in front of the occupant of the throne and will worship the one who lives to the ages of ages. They will throw their crowns before the throne and say:

notes.text: Jasper: in antiquity the name covered several precious stones, perhaps here a clear, bright stone (compare 21:11). *Carnelian*: Greek *sardion*, a red stone named after Sardis.
Rumbling: literally “voices.” Compare Exod 19:16.
In the center, around the throne: the meaning of the Greek is uncertain; perhaps “in the middle of each side of the throne.” Compare Ezek 1:5–25; 10:12.
Compare Ezek 1:10.
Isa 6:2–3, where the Hebrew has “Yahweh of Armies.”
Our Lord and God: a title also claimed by the emperor Domitian, according to Suetonius.

verses.text: In the right hand of him who sat on the throne I then saw a scroll with writing inside and on the reverse, sealed up with seven seals.{a}
I also saw a powerful angel announcing in a booming voice, “Who deserves to open the scroll and undo its seals?”
Yet nobody in the heavens, nor on the land, nor beneath the ground had the ability to unroll the scroll or peer into it.
I began to weep bitterly, because no one had been found who deserved to open the scroll or look inside it.{b}
But one of the elders told me, “Stop weeping. See, the lion from Judah’s tribe, David’s root, has won the victory; he can open the scroll with its seven seals.”{c}

Then, in the very center—with the throne and its four living creatures on one side and the elders on the other—I saw a Lamb standing, bearing the marks of slaughter. He had seven horns and seven eyes, and these are the seven spirits of God, commissioned to go out over all the earth.{d}
The Lamb came and took the scroll out of the right hand of him who sat on the throne.

As he took the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders prostrated themselves before the Lamb. Every one of them held a harp and golden bowls full of incense—the prayers of God’s holy people.

They sing a new song:
“You deserve to take the scroll
and open its seals,
since you were slaughtered, and with your blood you bought for God
people out of every tribe, language, nation, and people,{e}

and you made them into a kingdom, priests serving our God,
and they reign over the earth.”{f}
And I looked and heard a sound: many angels in a ring around the throne, around the living creatures, and around the elders. Their number was myriads upon myriads and thousands upon thousands,{g}

calling out in a great voice,
“The slaughtered Lamb deserves
to receive might and wealth, wisdom and strength,
honor and glory and praise!”

I heard, too, every creature that is in heaven, on the land, beneath the ground, and on the sea—everything in them—saying,
“Praise, honor, glory, and might
belong to him who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb,
for ever and ever!”{h}
And the four living creatures said, “Amen!” And the elders fell down and worshiped.{i}

notes.text: Compare Ezek 2:9–10; Isa 29:11.
I: Westcott and Hort bracket the emphatic pronoun.
Gen 49:9–10; Isa 11:1, 10. *Judah*: “praised” (Gen 29:35).
Seven spirits: Westcott and Hort bracket “seven.” Compare Isa 53:7; Zech 4:10.
Purchased for God: some manuscripts read “purchased us for God,” and Alexandrinus as reported lacks “for God.” *Those of every tribe*: literally “from every tribe.”
They reign: some manuscripts read “they will reign.” Later manuscripts read “made us … and we will reign.”
Myriads of myriads: literally “ten thousands of ten thousands”; compare Dan 7:10.
On the sea: Westcott and Hort bracket a Greek verb after these words.
Later manuscripts add “twenty-four” before “elders” and “him who lives forever and ever” after “worshiped.”

verses.text: Then I watched as the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures speak in a thunderous voice: “Come!”{a}
And I looked: a white horse, and its rider holding a bow! A crown was given him, and he rode forth as a conqueror, bent on conquest.
When he opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature say, “Come!”
Then another horse came out, red as fire, and its rider was given leave to take away peace from the earth and make people butcher one another; a huge sword was handed to him.{b}
When the third seal was opened by the Lamb, I heard the third living creature cry, “Come!” And what I saw was a black horse, and the rider on it held a pair of balances in his hand.
And I heard what sounded like a voice amid the four living beings, saying, “Wheat is a quart for a day’s wage, and barley is three quarts for a day’s wage; do not injure the oil and wine.”{c}
When he opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying, “Come!”

And there before me was a pale green horse, and the name of its rider was Death, and Hades came behind him. Authority was given to them over one quarter of the earth, to kill with the sword, with famine, with deadly disease, and through the wild beasts of the earth.{d}
When he opened the fifth seal, I saw beneath the altar the souls of people who had been put to death because of God’s word and because of the witness they maintained.
They shouted in a great voice: “Holy and true Master, how long until you give judgment and take vengeance for our blood upon the inhabitants of the earth?”{e}

Each of them received a white robe, and word came to them to take rest for a little time yet, until the count was complete of their fellow slaves and their brothers, those soon to be put to death, as they had been.{f}
Then he opened the sixth seal, and I watched. A great earthquake struck, the sun turned black like a sack woven of hair, and the full moon turned red as blood,{g}
Down to the earth fell the stars of heaven, like unripe figs flung from a fig tree when a strong wind shakes it.{h}
The sky was torn away like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island was shifted from its place.
Earth’s kings, its great men and its commanders, the wealthy and the mighty, every slave and every free person hid in caves and among mountain crags,{i}
and they call to the mountains and to the rocks: “Fall upon us and hide us from the face of the one seated on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb,{j}
for the great day of their anger has arrived, and who can remain standing?”{k}

notes.text: Come: later manuscripts read “Come and see”; so also in verses 3, 5 and 7.
Was given leave: Westcott and Hort bracket “to him” here and “from” before “the earth.”

Quart: Greek *choinix*, a dry measure of about 1 liter (just over a quart), roughly one person’s daily ration of grain. *A day’s wage*: Greek *dēnarion*, a Roman silver coin, the usual daily wage of a laborer (Matt 20:2). The prices are many times the normal rate, signifying famine.
The color of a corpse: Greek *chlōros*, “pale green.” *Pestilence*: literally “death.” Compare Ezek 14:21. Westcott and Hort bracket “it” after “its rider” and the article before “Death.”
Master: Greek *despotēs*.
Brothers: Greek *adelphoi*, which includes sisters. *Until the number was complete*: or “until their fellow slaves and brothers had completed their course.”
Compare Joel 2:10, 31; Isa 50:3.
Compare Isa 34:4.
Commanders: Greek *chiliarchoi*, “commanders of a thousand,” military tribunes.
Hos 10:8; compare Luke 23:30.
Their wrath: some manuscripts read “his wrath.” Compare Joel 2:11; Mal 3:2.

verses.text: After this I saw four angels standing on the earth’s four corners, holding back its four winds so that no wind would blow upon land, upon sea, or upon any tree.
And I saw a different angel ascending from the sunrise, carrying the living God’s seal; he called out in a great voice to the four angels who had received permission to injure earth and sea,
“Harm neither the earth nor the sea nor the trees, until we have sealed the foreheads of our God’s slaves.”{a}
And I heard how many were sealed: one hundred forty-four thousand, sealed out of every tribe of Israel’s descendants:
Out of Judah’s tribe twelve thousand sealed; out of Reuben’s, twelve thousand; out of Gad’s, twelve thousand;{b}
out of Asher’s, twelve thousand; out of Naphtali’s, twelve thousand; out of Manasseh’s, twelve thousand;{c}
out of Simeon’s, twelve thousand; out of Levi’s, twelve thousand; out of Issachar’s, twelve thousand;{d}
out of Zebulun’s, twelve thousand; out of Joseph’s, twelve thousand; out of Benjamin’s, twelve thousand sealed.{e}

After this I looked, and behold, a vast crowd that nobody could count, drawn from every nation, tribe, people, and language, stood in front of the throne and also before the Lamb. They were dressed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands,

And with a great shout they cry,
“Salvation is the gift of our God,
who sits upon the throne,
and of the Lamb!”
All the angels were standing in a circle about the throne, the elders and the four living creatures; and before the throne they fell face down and worshiped God,

and said,
“Amen! Praise and glory and wisdom,
thanks and honor,
might and strength,
belong to our God for ever and ever! Amen.”{f}
And one of the elders began to question me: “These who are wearing the white robes—who are they, and from where did they come?”
I replied, “My lord, you know.” He answered me, “These are the ones who are coming out of the great affliction. They have washed their robes and made them white in the Lamb’s blood.{g}

notes.text: Compare Ezek 9:4.
Reuben: “see, a son” (Gen 29:32). *Gad*: “fortune” (Gen 30:11). The list differs from the Old Testament lists of the tribes: Dan is missing, and Joseph and his son Manasseh both appear.
*Asher*: “happy” (Gen 30:13). *Naphtali*: “my wrestling” (Gen 30:8). *Manasseh*: “making to forget” (Gen 41:51).
*Simeon*: “he has heard” (Gen 29:33). *Levi*: “joined” (Gen 29:34). *Issachar*: “there is reward” (Gen 30:18).
*Zebulun*: “honor” or “dwelling” (Gen 30:20). *Joseph*: “may he add” (Gen 30:24). *Benjamin*: “son of the right hand” (Gen 35:18).
Amen: Westcott and Hort bracket the final “Amen.”
Compare Dan 12:1.
Spread his tent over them: that is, shelter them with his presence.
Ps 23:1–2; Isa 25:8. *Life-giving water*: literally “waters of life.”

verses.text: When he opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.{a}
And I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and seven trumpets were given to them.

And another angel came and stood by the altar with a gold incense pan. He was given a great amount of incense, in order to present it with the prayers of all the holy people at the golden altar before the throne.
And the smoke of the incense rose from the angel’s hand before God, along with the prayers of the holy people.
Then the angel picked up the censer, put into it some fire from the altar, and cast it down upon the land. Thunder rumbled, voices sounded, lightning flashed, and the ground shook.{b}
The seven angels with the seven trumpets now got ready to blow.

The first angel sounded his trumpet; hail and fire mingled with blood came down and was flung to the earth. One third of the earth burned up, one third of the trees burned up, and every blade of green grass burned up.{c}
The second angel sounded his trumpet, and what looked like a great burning mountain was thrown into the sea; one third of the sea became blood,
one third of the creatures in the sea that had life died, and one third of the ships were destroyed.
The third angel sounded, and down from heaven fell a huge star, flaming like a torch; it fell upon a third of the rivers and upon the springs.
The star is called Wormwood. A third of the water turned to wormwood, and many people died of the water, since it had turned bitter.{d}

The fourth angel sounded his trumpet. One third of the sun was struck, and one third of the moon, and one third of the stars, so that one third of them was darkened and the day lost one third of its light, and the night likewise.

Then, as I looked, I heard an eagle flying in midheaven call out in a great voice: “Woe! Woe! Woe to the earth’s inhabitants, on account of the other trumpet blasts about to be sounded by the three remaining angels!”{e}

notes.text: About half an hour: Greek *hōs hēmiōrion*, “about a half-hour.” The ancient hour was a twelfth of the daylight or of the night, and so varied in length with the season.
Compare Ezek 10:2. *Censer*: a pan for carrying burning coals and incense.
Compare Exod 9:23–25. *A third of the earth was burned up*: later manuscripts omit these words.
Wormwood: a plant with a very bitter taste (Greek *apsinthos*); compare Jer 9:15.
Eagle: later manuscripts read “angel.”

verses.text: The fifth angel sounded his trumpet, and I saw a star that had dropped from heaven to the earth. To the star was given the key of the pit of the abyss.{a}
It unlocked the shaft of the abyss, and up from the shaft billowed smoke like smoke from a huge furnace, and the sun and the air grew dark with the smoke from the shaft.
Locusts came down out of the smoke to the earth, and they were granted the kind of power that scorpions of the earth have.{b}
They were told to do no damage to the grass of the earth, or to any green plant or tree, but only to those people who lack God’s seal on their foreheads.
They were allowed not to kill them but to torment them five months, and their torment is like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a person.{c}
In those days people will search for death but will not discover it; they will yearn to die, and death will flee from them.
In appearance the locusts resembled horses made ready for war. They wore on their heads something like golden crowns, and they had faces like human faces.{d}
They had hair like women’s hair, and their teeth were like those of lions.{e}
Their chests were like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the thunder of many chariots with horses rushing into war.
Their tails are like those of scorpions, with stings, and the power to injure people for five months lies in their tails.
They have a king over them, the angel of the abyss; his name in Hebrew is Abaddon, but in Greek he has the name Apollyon.{f}
The first woe is past; two more woes are still to come after this.
The sixth angel sounded his trumpet, and I heard one voice coming from the corners of the golden altar that is in God’s presence,{g}
It said to the sixth angel, the trumpet holder: “Release the four angels who are held bound at the great river, the Euphrates.”{h}
And the four angels were let loose, who stood ready for that precise hour and day and month and year, to kill one third of humanity.{i}
The number of the mounted troops was two hundred million; I heard what their number was.{j}

This is how the horses and their riders looked in my vision: the riders wore breastplates of fiery red, deep blue, and brimstone yellow. The horses had heads like lions’ heads, and fire, smoke, and brimstone streamed from their mouths.{k}
These three plagues, the fire and smoke and sulfur pouring from the horses’ mouths, killed a third of humankind.
The horses’ power lies in their mouths and in their tails as well, for their tails look like serpents and have heads, and by means of them they inflict injury.

The people who remained, who had not been killed in these plagues, nevertheless did not repent of what their hands had made, nor stop worshiping the demons and the golden, silver, bronze, stone and wooden idols, which have no power to see, to hear or to walk.{l}
Nor did they turn away from their murders, their sorceries, their sexual immorality or their thefts.{m}

notes.text: Abyss: Greek *abyssos*, “bottomless,” the deep underworld prison of hostile spirits.
Compare Exod 10:12–15; Joel 1–2.
Five months: roughly the life span of a locust.
Compare Joel 2:4–5.
Compare Joel 1:6.
Abaddon: Hebrew for “destruction,” a name for the realm of the dead (Job 26:6; Prov 15:11). *Apollyon*: Greek for “destroyer,” perhaps also a play on the name of the god Apollo.
Four horns: Westcott and Hort read only “the horns”; many manuscripts add “four.”
Euphrates: the great river of Mesopotamia, the eastern frontier of the Roman world; the name perhaps means “fruitful.”
That hour: not a time of day but the appointed moment; Greek *eis tēn hōran*, “for the hour.” The single article governs all four nouns, pointing to one fixed time.
Two hundred million: Greek *dismyriades myriadōn*, “twice ten thousand times ten thousand.”
Dark blue: Greek *hyakinthinos*, the color of the hyacinth, a deep blue or violet. *Sulfur*: Greek *theion*, traditionally “brimstone.”
Sorceries: Greek *pharmaka*, “drugs,” “potions,” “spells.”

verses.text: Then I saw another mighty angel descending from heaven. A cloud was wrapped around him, a rainbow crowned his head, his face was like the sun, and his legs were like pillars of fire.{a}
He had a small scroll in his hand, unrolled. Then he placed his right foot on the sea and his left on the land,
and cried out with a great voice, as a lion roars. And when he cried out, the seven thunders uttered their voices.
When the seven thunders spoke, I was on the point of writing, but I heard a voice out of heaven saying, “Put a seal on what the seven thunders said; do not write it down.”{b}
Then the angel I had seen standing upon the sea and upon the land lifted up his right hand to heaven

and took an oath by the One who lives to the ages of the ages, the maker of heaven and all it holds, of the earth and all it holds, and of the sea and all it holds: “Time is up; there will be no more waiting.{c}
but in the days of the seventh angel’s voice, when he is about to sound his trumpet, the hidden purpose of God will be completed, just as he announced to his slaves the prophets.”{d}
The voice I had heard out of heaven was speaking to me once more, and it said, “Go and take the scroll that lies unrolled on the hand of the angel who is standing on the sea and on the land.”
And I went to that angel and asked him for the little scroll. “Here, take it and eat it,” he replied. “It will embitter your belly, yet in your mouth it will be as sweet as honey.”{e}
I took the small scroll from the angel’s hand and ate it up. In my mouth it tasted sweet as honey, yet once I had eaten it, my stomach turned bitter.
Then I was told, “Once more you have to prophesy, concerning many peoples, nations, languages and kings.”{f}

notes.text: Legs: literally “feet.”
Compare Dan 8:26; 12:4, 9.
Dan 12:7; compare Deut 32:40. *Of the sea and all it holds*: Westcott and Hort bracket these words. *No more waiting*: literally “time will no longer be.”
Compare Amos 3:7.
Concerning: or “against.”

verses.text: I was given a measuring rod like a staff, and told, “Rise, and measure God’s temple and the altar, and count the people who worship in it.{a}
But the outer court of the temple, leave it out and do not measure it, since it was given over to the nations, who will trample down the holy city for forty-two months.{b}
I will empower my two witnesses, and clothed in sackcloth they will prophesy during one thousand two hundred sixty days.”{c}
These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth.{d}
Should any enemy try to injure them, flames stream out of their mouths and devour the foes; in just that way every would-be attacker is doomed to die.{e}

These two possess the power to close up heaven, so that during the span of their prophesying no showers come down; they also command the waters, changing them to blood, and can afflict the land with plagues of every sort as often as they like.{f}
When their witnessing is finished, the beast coming up from the bottomless pit will battle them, defeat them, and put them to death.{g}
And their corpses will lie in the broad street of the great city, which is called, in a spiritual sense, Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord also was crucified.{h}
For three and a half days people from every people, tribe, language and nation gaze at their corpses and refuse to let them be laid in a tomb.
Those who live on the earth gloat over them and celebrate and exchange gifts, because these two prophets had tormented the inhabitants of the earth.
After three and a half days, however, life-giving breath from God entered them. They rose upright, and terror gripped the people looking on.{i}
And they heard a mighty voice out of heaven say to them, “Come up here!” And in a cloud they went up into heaven, while their enemies looked on.{j}
In that same hour a great earthquake struck, and a tenth of the city collapsed; the earthquake killed seven thousand persons. The rest were filled with fear and gave glory to the God of heaven.{k}
The second woe is past; look, the third woe is coming quickly.

The seventh angel sounded the trumpet. Loud voices were heard in heaven, declaring,
“The kingdom of the world has become
the possession of our Lord and of his Christ,
and he shall be king through all the ages.”{l}
And the twenty-four elders, who sit on their thrones before God, prostrated themselves, faces to the ground, and worshiped God,{m}

saying,
“We give you thanks, Lord God Almighty,
the one who is and who was,
because you have taken up your great power
and have begun your reign.{n}

Furious were the nations,
and now your anger has arrived,
the moment for judging the dead,
for paying their reward to your slaves the prophets,
to the saints, and to all who revere your name,
the lowly and the great alike,
and for ruining the ruiners of the earth.”{o}
Then the temple of God in heaven was thrown open, and inside it the ark of his covenant came into view, and there came lightning and rumbling and thunder, an earthquake and a great hailstorm.

notes.text: Reed: a measuring rod; compare Ezek 40:3; Zech 2:1–2. *Was told*: literally “saying.”

Forty-two months: this equals three and a half years, the span named in Dan 7:25; 12:7; compare verse 3 and 12:6, 14; 13:5. Westcott and Hort bracket “and” in the Greek number. *Omit*: literally “cast out outside.” *The nations*: or “the Gentiles.”
Twelve hundred and sixty days: the same span as forty-two months, counting thirty days to a month.
Zech 4:3, 11–14, where the Hebrew has *ʾadon*, “lord,” not the divine name.
Compare Jer 5:14; 2 Kgs 1:10–12.
Compare 1 Kgs 17:1; Exod 7:17–20.
Compare Dan 7:3, 7, 21.
In prophetic language: literally “spiritually.” *Sodom*: perhaps “burning.” *Egypt*: from the Greek *Aigyptos*; the Hebrew name is *Mitsrayim*.
Ezek 37:5, 10. Westcott and Hort bracket “the” before “three” and “into” before “them.”
Compare 2 Kgs 2:11.
At that very hour: not a clock time but “at that moment.” *Seven thousand people*: literally “names of people, seven thousand.”
Ps 2:2. *Christ*: Greek *Christos*, “anointed one,” translating the Hebrew *mashiaḥ*, “Messiah.”
Who sit: Westcott and Hort bracket the article before “before God.”
Who are and who were: later manuscripts add “and who are coming.” *Lord God Almighty*: see the note on 1:8.

verses.text: A great sign was seen in heaven: a woman wrapped in the sun, with the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars on her head.
She was pregnant, and she was crying out in labor, in anguish to give birth.
Another sign was seen in heaven as well: a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and wearing seven royal crowns on its heads.{a}

Its tail dragged down a third of heaven’s stars and flung them onto the earth. The dragon took its stand before the woman who was about to give birth, in order to swallow her child as soon as it was born.{b}
And she bore a child, a son, who is destined to govern every nation with a rod of iron. Her child, though, was caught up to God and to his throne.{c}
The woman herself fled into the wilderness, to a spot God had prepared for her, where she would be fed for twelve hundred sixty days.
A battle then broke out in heaven. Michael and his angels waged war against the dragon, and the dragon with his angels fought back,{d}
but they lost the battle, and heaven had room for them no longer.
and the great dragon was cast out: that primeval serpent, called the Devil and Satan, who leads the whole world astray. It was cast down to the earth, and its angels were cast down with it.{e}

They overcame him by the Lamb’s blood
and by the word of their testimony,
and did not love their lives, even when facing death.

So be glad, you heavens,
and all who make your home in them!
But woe to the earth and to the sea,
because the devil has descended to you
in great fury, aware that his time is short!”{g}
On seeing that it had been cast down to the earth, the dragon went in pursuit of the woman, the one who had borne the male child.

Yet the woman received the two wings of the great eagle, to fly away into the wilderness, to the place prepared for her, where she is fed for a season, two seasons, and half a season, out of the serpent’s sight.{h}
And from its mouth the serpent poured out water after the woman, like a river, to sweep her away with the flood.
The earth, however, rescued the woman. It opened its mouth and gulped down the river that the dragon had spouted from its own mouth.
Furious at the woman, the dragon went away to wage war against the others among her children, those who obey the commands of God and bear the witness of Jesus.{i}

notes.text: Diadems: royal crowns, as distinct from the victor’s wreath (Greek *stephanos*). Compare Dan 7:7.
Compare Dan 8:10.
Michael: Hebrew “who is like God?”; the angelic prince of Dan 10:13, 21; 12:1.
Ancient serpent: compare Gen 3:1–15.
Brothers: Greek *adelphoi*, which includes sisters. *Accuser*: compare Job 1:6–11; Zech 3:1.
Compare Isa 44:23; 49:13.
Dan 7:25; 12:7; that is, three and a half years. *Two times*: literally “times.” Compare Exod 19:4.
Children: literally “seed.”

verses.text: And it took its stand on the sand of the seashore. ¶Out of the sea I saw a beast emerging; it had ten horns and seven heads, a diadem on each of its ten horns, and names of blasphemy on its heads.{a}
The creature I saw looked like a leopard, with paws like a bear’s and a mouth like a lion’s. The dragon gave it his own power and throne, along with extensive authority.{b}
One of its heads looked as if it had been slaughtered to death, but its deadly wound was healed, and the whole earth went after the beast in amazement.{c}
They worshiped the dragon because it had given the authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast as well, asking, “Who is like the beast, and who can wage war against it?”{d}
It received a mouth that spoke arrogant words and blasphemy, and it received authority to act for forty-two months.{e}
It opened its mouth to speak slanders against God, to curse his name and his tent, those who live in heaven.{f}
Leave was given it, too, to make war on the saints and defeat them, and to hold power over every tribe, people, tongue and nation.{g}
Every inhabitant of the earth will worship it, all those whose names were not recorded, from the world’s founding, in the book of life belonging to the slaughtered Lamb.{h}
If anyone has an ear, let him listen:
Then I saw a second beast ascending from the earth, with two horns like those of a lamb, yet it spoke like a dragon.
It wields all the authority of the first beast, acting before its eyes, and it causes the earth and those living on it to worship the first beast, the one whose deadly wound had been healed.{j}
It performs great signs, even bringing fire down out of heaven onto the earth in full view of everyone.{k}
Through the signs it was permitted to do before the beast, it misleads those living on the earth, instructing them to fashion an image of the beast who had received the sword stroke and yet lived.
It was also permitted to impart a spirit to the beast’s statue, so that the statue itself would talk and would bring about the execution of all who would not bow before it.{l}
Everyone, the lowly and the mighty, the wealthy and the needy, the free and the enslaved, it compels to receive a mark on the right hand or the forehead,{m}
so that nobody can buy or sell without having the mark—the name of the beast or the number that stands for its name.{n}
Here is wisdom: whoever has insight should calculate the beast’s number, for it stands for a person; its number is 666.{o}

notes.text: And it took its stand on the sand of the seashore: many modern editions number these words 12:18. *It* is the dragon; later manuscripts read “I stood,” attaching the words to John’s vision. *Names of blasphemy*: some manuscripts read “a name of blasphemy.” Compare Dan 7:2–7.
Compare Dan 7:4–6.
Slaughtered to death: the same Greek word that is used of the Lamb in 5:6.
Compare Exod 15:11.
Compare Dan 7:8, 11, 20, 25. Westcott and Hort bracket “and” in the Greek number.
His tent: that is, his dwelling place. Later manuscripts read “his tent and those who live in heaven.”
Leave was given it, too, to make war on the saints and defeat them: Westcott and Hort bracket these words, which P47, Alexandrinus and Ephraemi omit. Compare Dan 7:21.

Since the founding of the world: these words may instead go with “slain,” “the Lamb slain since the founding of the world”; compare 17:8. *Everyone whose name*: literally “whose name,” in the singular.

Jer 15:2; 43:11. *Kills*: Westcott and Hort read “will kill”; Alexandrinus, as reported, reads “is to be killed,” which would yield the sense that anyone fated to be slain by the sword is slain by it. *Here the saints are called to*: literally “here is the endurance and the faith of the saints.”
On its behalf: literally “before it,” “in its presence.”
Compare 1 Kgs 18:38.
Breath: or “spirit.” Westcott and Hort bracket the Greek conjunction before “everyone.” Compare Dan 3:5–6.
Mark: Greek *charagma*, a brand or stamp; the word was also used of the impression on coins and official seals.
So that: Westcott and Hort bracket “and” before these words.

Work out: literally “count,” “reckon,” using the ancient practice of giving each letter a numerical value (gematria). *A human number*: or “the number of a person.” *Six hundred and sixty-six*: so Westcott and Hort and most manuscripts. P115 (3rd–4th century), Codex Ephraemi and some others read “six hundred and sixteen,” and Irenaeus (about AD 180) knew of copies with that number. Both totals can be obtained from the Hebrew letters of “Nero Caesar” in different spellings, though many other solutions have been proposed.

verses.text: I looked, and the Lamb was there, standing on Mount Zion! Along with him, 144,000 people bore on their foreheads his name and the name of his Father.{a}
And out of heaven I heard a sound like the rushing of great waters and like loud thunder rolling; the voice that I heard was like that of harpists accompanying themselves on their harps.

They sing what seems a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders. And none was able to learn the song except for those 144,000 who have been bought out of the earth.

They are the ones who kept themselves unsoiled by women, being virgins; they are the followers of the Lamb, going wherever he leads. They were bought out of humanity as firstfruits offered to God and to the Lamb,{b}
and in their speech no lie was found; they are without blemish.{c}
Next I saw another angel in flight high overhead, bringing an everlasting gospel to announce to earth’s inhabitants, to every nation, tribe, tongue and people.{d}
With a loud voice he said, “Fear God and give him glory, for the hour of his judgment has arrived. Worship the maker of heaven and earth, of the sea and the springs of water.”{e}
Another angel, a second, followed and said, “She has fallen! Fallen is Babylon the great, who gave all the nations a drink of the wine of her raging immorality!”{f}
Next, a third angel came after them, saying in a mighty voice, “If anyone worships the beast and its statue, and gets a mark on his forehead or on his hand,
he too will drink the wine of God’s anger, mixed full strength in the cup of his wrath. He will be tortured in fire and brimstone before the holy angels and before the Lamb.{g}
The smoke of their torment goes up forever and ever. Day and night there is no rest for those who worship the beast and its image, or for anyone who takes the mark of its name.”{h}
Here is the call for endurance on the part of the holy people, who keep God’s commandments and the faith of Jesus.{i}

And I heard a voice speak from heaven: “Write: Blessed from this moment are the dead who die in the Lord.” “Yes,” the Spirit says, “let them find relief from their labors, for their deeds accompany them.”{j}
As I watched, a white cloud appeared, and on it sat someone resembling a son of man; on his head was a crown of gold, and in his hand a keen-edged sickle.{k}

And a different angel emerged from the temple, shouting with a powerful voice to the one who sat upon the cloud: “Send out your sickle and harvest, for the hour to harvest has come, because the earth’s crop has dried out.”{l}
He who sat on the cloud cast his sickle onto the earth, and the earth’s harvest was gathered in.
Out of the heavenly temple came yet another angel, and he as well held a keen-edged sickle.

And from the altar there came out yet another angel, who has charge over the fire. He called out with a strong voice to the holder of the sharp sickle, “Send out your sharp sickle and collect the clusters of grapes on the earth’s vine, for its grapes have reached full ripeness.”{m}
The angel cast his sickle onto the earth and harvested its grapes, flinging them into the vast winepress of God’s fury.
Outside the city the grapes were trampled in the press, and out of it poured blood, rising to the horses’ bridles, across a distance of about 180 miles.{n}

notes.text: Zion: the hill of Jerusalem’s temple, and a name for the city; perhaps “fortress.” *His name and*: later manuscripts omit these words.
Virgins: Greek *parthenoi*, here masculine, perhaps picturing holy-war purity (compare Deut 23:9–10; 1 Sam 21:5) or faithfulness to God in contrast with spiritual prostitution.
Compare Zeph 3:13; Isa 53:9. Later manuscripts add “before the throne of God.”
Gospel: Greek *euangelion*, “good news.” *Another*: some manuscripts omit this word.
The hour: the appointed time, not a time of day. Compare Exod 20:11; Ps 146:6.

Isa 21:9; Jer 51:7–8. *Babylon*: the Greek form of the Hebrew *Bavel*; the Akkadian *Bab-ili* means “gate of god,” while Gen 11:9 links it with Hebrew *balal*, “confuse.” Here it is a code name for a great city, probably Rome (compare 1 Pet 5:13). *Passionate immorality*: literally “the wine of the passion of her immorality”; the Greek *thymos* can mean both “passion” and “wrath.” *A second angel*: Westcott and Hort bracket “angel.”
Compare Isa 51:17; Jer 25:15; Gen 19:24.
Compare Isa 34:10.
The faith of Jesus: or “their faith in Jesus,” or “faithfulness to Jesus.”
From now on: the Greek *ap’ arti* may instead go with what follows: “From now on, yes, says the Spirit.”
Ripe: literally “dried,” that is, fully ripe. Compare Joel 3:13.
Came: Westcott and Hort bracket this verb and the article before “who has authority.” *Authority over the fire*: compare 8:3–5.
About 180 miles: Greek “1,600 stadia,” about 300 km; a stadion was about 607 feet (185 m). The number may be symbolic (40 × 40, or 4 × 4 × 100). Compare Isa 63:1–6; Joel 3:13.

verses.text: And I saw another portent in heaven, large and astonishing: seven angels holding the seven final plagues, since by them God’s wrath is completed.
I also saw what looked like a glassy sea mingled with fire, and the victors over the beast, over its likeness, and over its name’s number stood beside the glassy sea, holding God’s harps.{a}

They are chanting the song of Moses, God’s slave, and the song of the Lamb:
“Mighty and astonishing are the things you do,
O Lord God, Ruler over all!
Upright and true are your paths,
King of the ages!{b}

Lord, who will fail to fear you
and give glory to your name?
You alone are holy.
Every nation will come
and bow low before you,
for your judgments stand revealed.”{c}
After these things I saw it: the sanctuary of the tent of testimony in heaven was opened,{d}
and the seven angels holding the seven plagues emerged from it, clothed in stone, pure and shining, and wearing gold sashes about their breasts.{e}
Then one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God, who lives forever and ever.
And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from his power, and no one could enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.{f}

notes.text: Beside: or “on.” *Harps of God*: that is, harps given by God, or harps for the worship of God.

Exod 15:1–18; Deut 32:4; Ps 111:2; 139:14. *Moses*: explained in Exod 2:10 by Hebrew *mashah*, “draw out.” *Lord God Almighty*: see the note on 1:8. *King of the ages*: so Westcott and Hort, with P47 and Sinaiticus as first written; Alexandrinus and many others read “King of the nations,” and later manuscripts “King of the saints.”
Jer 10:7; Ps 86:9; Mal 1:11. In Jer 10:7 the Hebrew has no divine name; in Ps 86:9 it has *ʾAdonay*, “Lord.”
Tent of testimony: the tabernacle (Exod 38:21; 40:34–35 in the Greek Old Testament).

Clothed in stone: so Westcott and Hort, following Alexandrinus and Ephraemi, perhaps picturing robes set with precious stones (compare Ezek 28:13). Many manuscripts read *linon*, “linen,” for *lithon*, “stone.” Westcott and Hort bracket the article before “with the seven plagues.”
Compare Exod 40:34–35; 1 Kgs 8:10–11; Isa 6:4.

verses.text: A loud voice from the temple then called to the seven angels, “Go, empty the seven bowls of God’s fury onto the earth.”
The first angel went off and emptied his bowl onto the land, and ugly, festering sores appeared on those who wore the beast’s mark and bowed down to its image.{a}
Then the second angel emptied his bowl into the sea, and the water turned into blood like a dead man’s, and every living creature in the sea perished.{b}
Then the third emptied his bowl into the rivers and the water sources, and these turned into blood.
The fourth emptied his bowl onto the sun, and the sun was permitted to burn people with its fire.
People were seared by tremendous heat, and they cursed God’s name—the God who holds power over these plagues—and refused to repent and to glorify him.
Then the fifth emptied his bowl onto the throne of the beast, and its realm was darkened. People chewed their tongues in anguish{e}
and reviled the God of heaven for their sufferings and sores, yet they did not repent of their works.
Then the sixth emptied his bowl onto the great Euphrates River. Its water dried up, so that a road lay ready for the kings from the east.{f}
And from the dragon’s mouth, from the mouth of the beast, and from the mouth of the false prophet, I watched three unclean spirits emerge, which resembled frogs.{g}
These are spirits of demons that do signs; they travel out to the rulers of the entire world to gather them for the war of that great day belonging to God, the Almighty.
(“Notice, I come as a thief does! Happy is the one who stays alert and holds on to his clothing, so that he need not walk naked and have his shame seen.”)
And they gathered the kings together at the place that is called Harmagedon in Hebrew.{h}
The seventh angel emptied his bowl upon the air, and from the sanctuary, from the throne, a great voice called, “It is finished!”{i}
Lightning flashed, there was rumbling and thunder, and a great earthquake struck, the like of which had not happened since humans first lived on the earth, so violent was the quake.{j}
The great city broke into three pieces, and the nations’ cities collapsed. Babylon the great came to mind before God, and he made her drink the cup brimming with the wine of his fierce anger.
Every island vanished; the mountains were nowhere to be seen.
And great hailstones, weighing about a talent, fell from the sky upon people, and people blasphemed God because of the plague of hail; for that plague was extremely severe.{k}

notes.text: Compare Exod 9:9–11.
Compare Exod 7:17–21.
The Holy One: Westcott and Hort bracket the article. Later manuscripts read “and who will be.”
Lord God, the Almighty: see the note on 1:8. Compare Ps 19:9.
Compare Exod 10:21–23.
From the east: literally “from the rising of the sun.” Westcott and Hort bracket the article before “Euphrates.” Compare Isa 11:15; Jer 50:38.
Compare Exod 8:2–7.
Harmagedon: traditionally “Armageddon”; probably Hebrew *har Megiddo*, “mountain of Megiddo,” the site of famous battles (Judg 5:19; 2 Kgs 23:29). Some manuscripts read “Mageddon.”
From the throne: later manuscripts read “of heaven, from the throne.”
Compare Dan 12:1.
About seventy pounds: literally “about a talent’s weight”; the talent was the largest ancient unit of weight, about 30–35 kg (65–75 pounds), though its value varied. Compare Exod 9:23–25.

verses.text: Then there came one of the seven angels who had been carrying the seven bowls, and he told me, “Come along! I will let you see the condemnation of the notorious prostitute who sits beside the many waters,{a}
the one with whom earth’s kings have committed immorality, and with the wine of whose immorality the earth’s inhabitants have grown drunk.”
In the Spirit he took me away to a wilderness. There I noticed a woman seated upon a scarlet beast that was covered with blasphemous names and had seven heads and ten horns.
The woman wore purple and scarlet, and was resplendent with gold, jewels, and pearls. A gold cup brimming with detestable things and with the foulness of her immorality was in her hand.{b}
Across her forehead a name was written, a mystery: “Babylon the great, mother of the prostitutes and of the abominations of the earth.”{c}
The woman, I noticed, was drunk with the blood of the holy people and with the blood of Jesus’s witnesses. And when I saw her, I wondered greatly.{d}
The angel said, “Why do you wonder? Let me explain the secret of the woman, and of the beast that bears her, which has seven heads and ten horns.

The beast that you saw existed once and exists no longer; it is going to rise from the abyss and then head for ruin. Earth’s inhabitants whose names have not, since the world was founded, been entered in the book of life will marvel at the sight of the beast, because it existed once, exists no longer, and yet will appear.{e}
Here is something that calls for a mind with insight: the seven heads stand for seven hills, where the woman has her seat. They also stand for seven kings;{f}
five are fallen, one is living, and the last has still to come; and whenever he comes, he is to remain a little while.
As for the beast that once was and now is not, it is itself an eighth, but it springs from the seven, and it is heading for destruction.
The ten horns that you saw are ten kings. They have not yet received a kingdom, but for a single hour they receive authority as kings alongside the beast.{g}
They share a single purpose, and they surrender their might and their authority to the beast.
These will fight against the Lamb, yet the Lamb will triumph over them, because Lord of lords he is, and King of kings; and with him are the called, the chosen, and the faithful ones.”{h}
He says to me: “Those waters that you saw, on which the prostitute is seated, stand for peoples and crowds and nations and languages.
And the ten horns you saw, along with the beast—they will hate the prostitute, strip her of everything and leave her naked, eat her flesh, and burn what remains of her with fire.{i}
It is God who has moved their hearts to accomplish his intention, to act with one accord and yield their royal power to the beast until what God has spoken comes to pass.
The woman you saw is the great city that holds sovereignty over the kings of the earth.”

notes.text: Beside many waters: compare Jer 51:13, of Babylon on the Euphrates and its canals.
Compare Jer 51:7.
A mystery: or “a name of mystery,” that is, a symbolic name.
Witnesses: Greek *martyres*, the source of the English word “martyrs.”
Compare Dan 7:3.
Mountains: Greek *orē*, “mountains” or “hills”; Rome was famous as the city of seven hills. *They are also seven kings*: in the Greek these words begin verse 10.
For a single hour: that is, for a very short time. Compare Dan 7:24.
Compare Deut 10:17; Dan 2:47.
In fire: Westcott and Hort bracket the Greek preposition.

verses.text: After these things I saw a different angel coming down out of heaven. He possessed great authority, and the earth shone with his glory.{a}

He shouted in a mighty voice:
“Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great!
She has turned into a dwelling for demons,
a lockup for every unclean spirit,
a lockup for every unclean and loathsome bird,
and a lockup for every unclean and loathsome beast.{b}

For from the wine of her passionate immorality
all the nations have drunk,
and the kings of the earth fornicated with her,
and the merchants of the earth grew rich
from the power of her luxury.”{c}

Another voice from heaven I heard, crying,
“My people, leave her,
so you take no part in her sins
and no portion of her plagues;{d}

For her sins have piled up to the sky,
and God has recalled her crimes.{e}

Therefore, in a single day her plagues will arrive:
pestilence, mourning, and famine,
and she will be consumed by fire,
for strong is the Lord God who has judged her.”{h}
The kings of the earth, who were immoral with her and shared her luxury, will weep and mourn over her as they see the smoke of her burning.

Keeping their distance for terror at her torment, they will cry,
“Alas, alas, great city,
Babylon, city of might!
In a single hour your doom has fallen!”{i}
And the merchants of the earth are weeping and mourning over her, because nobody buys their merchandise any longer:{j}

a cargo of gold, silver, jewels, and pearls; of fine linen, purple cloth, silk, and scarlet; of all kinds of citron wood and every article of ivory; of every article of expensive wood, and of bronze, iron, and marble;{k}
and cinnamon, spices, incense, perfume, and frankincense; and wine, oil, fine flour, and grain; and cattle and sheep and horses and carriages; and bodies—that is, human souls.{l}

“The ripe fruit you craved with all your soul
has left you,
and all your rich and dazzling things
are lost to you,
and never again will people find them.”{m}
Those who traded in these goods and made their fortunes from her will keep their distance, terrified at her torment, crying and mourning,

saying,
“Alas, alas, that great city,
which wore fine linen, purple, and scarlet,
and was gilded with gold,
with precious stones and pearls!{n}
In a single hour such great wealth was devastated!” ¶Every shipmaster, everyone sailing to any destination, the sailors, and all who make their living from the sea remained at a distance{o}
and shouted, as they saw the smoke rising from her burning, “Which city was like this great city?”{p}

They flung dust on their heads, crying and mourning, and they shouted,
“Alas, alas, great city,
whose costly wealth made rich
all who owned ships at sea!
In a single hour she is ruined.”{q}

Then one mighty angel picked up a boulder like a huge millstone and flung it into the sea, with these words:
“Just so, in a violent plunge,
Babylon the great city will be hurled down,
and nobody will find her again.{s}

In her the blood of prophets and of holy people was found,
together with the blood of everyone slaughtered on earth.”

notes.text: Compare Ezek 43:2.

Isa 21:9; 13:21; 34:11–15; Jer 50:39. *Prison*: or “lair.” *And a prison for every foul and hated beast*: so Alexandrinus and some other manuscripts; Westcott and Hort place these words in the margin and read “a prison for every foul and hated bird.”
Have fallen: so Westcott and Hort; many manuscripts read “have drunk.” *Wine*: Westcott and Hort bracket “the wine.”
Compare Jer 51:9.
Jer 50:29; Ps 137:8. Westcott and Hort bracket the article before “double.”
Single day: compare Isa 47:9. *The Lord God*: Westcott and Hort bracket “Lord.” Compare Jer 50:34, where the Hebrew has *Yahweh*.
Alas: Greek *ouai*, translated “woe” elsewhere. *In a single hour*: that is, suddenly; not a clock time. So also verses 17 and 19.
Compare Ezek 27:1–36, the lament over Tyre.
Citron wood: a fragrant North African wood prized for luxury tables.

Spice: Greek *amōmon*, an aromatic plant from India. *Ointment*: Greek *myron*, perfumed oil. *Bodies*: Greek *sōmata*, a common term for slaves in commercial documents. *Even human lives*: literally “and souls of people”; compare Ezek 27:13.
No one will find them: literally “they will never find them.”
With gold: Westcott and Hort bracket the Greek preposition.
Everyone who sails anywhere: literally “everyone sailing to a place”; later manuscripts read “all the company on ships.”
Compare Ezek 27:32.
Compare Ezek 27:30.
Has given judgment for you against her: literally “has judged your judgment from her.” Compare Deut 32:43.
Compare Jer 51:63–64.
Of any trade: Westcott and Hort bracket these words. Compare Ezek 26:13; Jer 25:10.
Jer 7:34; 16:9; 25:10; Isa 23:8. Westcott and Hort bracket the article before “merchants.”

verses.text:
because true and just are his judgments.
He condemned the great prostitute,
the one who corrupted the earth by her immorality,
and he has taken vengeance on her for the blood of his slaves.”{b}

The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell prostrate and worshiped the God seated on the throne, saying,
“Amen! Hallelujah!”{d}

A voice came out of the throne, and it said,
“Give praise to our God,
all his slaves,
and those who fear him,
the small and the great.”{e}

Then I heard what seemed the voice of an immense multitude, like the sound of rushing water and like the rumble of loud thunder, saying,
“Hallelujah!
Because the Lord our God,
the Almighty, has taken up his reign.{f}

and she was given clothing
of bright, clean fine linen to wear.”
(The fine linen, you see, stands for the righteous deeds of the holy people.)
Then he told me, “Write: Blessed are the people invited to the marriage banquet of the Lamb!” And he told me, “These words are God’s own truth.”{h}

I threw myself down in front of his feet to worship him. But he told me, “Never do that! I am only a slave like you and your brothers who maintain the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! The testimony about Jesus is what inspires prophecy.”{i}
Then I saw heaven standing open, and a white horse appeared. Its rider is named Faithful and True, and he judges and wages war in righteousness.{j}
His eyes blaze like fire, and many diadems are on his head. A name is inscribed on him that no one understands but he himself.{k}
He is clothed in a robe sprinkled with blood, and his name is called the Word of God.{l}
Heaven’s armies rode behind him on white horses, dressed in pure white linen.

A sharp sword extends from his mouth, so that with it he may strike the nations; he will shepherd them with a rod of iron. And he himself treads the winepress that holds the fierce wrath of God the Almighty.{m}
The title “King of kings and Lord of lords” is inscribed upon his cloak, on his thigh.
Then I noticed an angel standing in the sun. He called out in a mighty voice to every bird that flies across midheaven: “Come, assemble for God’s great banquet,{n}
so that you may eat the flesh of kings, of generals, and of the strong; the flesh of horses and of those who sit on them; and the flesh of everyone, free and slave, small and great.”{o}
I saw the beast as well, and earth’s kings and their armies, mustered to do battle with the horse’s rider and his army.

The beast was seized, and so was the false prophet who had done the signs in its presence, signs that had misled those who took the beast’s mark and bowed down to its image. Both of them were flung alive into the fiery lake that blazes with sulfur.
All the others were slain by the sword that issues from the rider’s mouth, and every bird ate its fill of their flesh.

notes.text: Hallelujah: Hebrew *halelu-yah*, “praise Yah,” *Yah* being a short form of *Yahweh*. In the New Testament the word occurs only in this chapter (verses 1, 3, 4, 6).
Deut 32:43; 2 Kgs 9:7. *On her*: literally “from her hand.”
Our God: Westcott and Hort bracket “our.” *The Lord our God, the Almighty*: see the note on 1:8. Compare Ps 93:1; 97:1, where the Hebrew has *Yahweh*.
Bride: literally “wife.”
The angel: Greek “he”; compare 17:1.
Brothers: Greek *adelphoi*, which includes sisters. *The testimony of Jesus*: either the witness Jesus gave, or the witness borne to him.
Is called: Westcott and Hort bracket this word. Compare Isa 11:4.
Later manuscripts add “names written and” before “a name written.”
Sprinkled: so Westcott and Hort, following some manuscripts; Alexandrinus and most others read “dipped in.” Compare Isa 63:1–3.
Ps 2:9; Isa 11:4; 63:3. Later manuscripts read “two-edged sword.”
With a loud voice: Westcott and Hort bracket the Greek preposition.
Ezek 39:17–20. *Commanders*: see the note on 6:15.

verses.text: And I saw an angel come down from heaven; in his hand he held the key of the abyss, together with a massive chain.
He seized the dragon, that ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan, and bound him fast for a thousand years.{a}

He flung it into the abyss, closed it up, and set a seal over it, so that it could no longer mislead the nations until the thousand years should be completed. After that it must be let loose for a short while.

I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given to them. I saw too the souls of those beheaded for the testimony of Jesus and for the word of God, and of those who did not bow to the beast or to its image, and did not accept the mark upon their forehead and upon their hand. They lived and ruled with Christ a thousand years.{b}
The rest of the dead had no new life until the thousand years ended. This is the first resurrection.

Blessed—and holy—are those who have a place in the first resurrection. Over them the second death holds no authority; instead they will be priests belonging to God and to Christ, and for those thousand years they will reign with him.{c}
When the thousand years have run their course, Satan will be released from his prison.
He will go out to mislead the nations at the earth’s four corners, Gog and Magog, and to muster them for battle; they are as countless as the sand along the sea.{d}
They advanced over the breadth of the earth and besieged the camp of the holy people, the city that he loves. Then fire fell from heaven and consumed them.{e}

As for the devil who had led them astray, he was cast into the lake of burning sulfur, in which the beast and the false prophet are also found; there they will be in torment by day and by night through all the ages.
Then I saw a great white throne, with the one seated upon it. Earth and heaven fled from his face, and no place could be found for them.

And I saw the dead, important and unimportant alike, standing before the throne. Scrolls were unrolled; then another scroll was unrolled—the scroll of life. By the contents of the scrolls the dead were judged, each according to his deeds.{f}
The sea yielded up the dead it held; Death and Hades yielded up the dead they held; and each person was judged by what he had done.
Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire.{g}
Whoever was not listed in the scroll of life was hurled into the pool of fire.

notes.text: A thousand years: Latin *millennium*; so also in verses 3–7.
Beheaded: literally “executed with the axe.” Compare Dan 7:9, 22.
For the thousand years: Westcott and Hort bracket “the.”
Gog and Magog: compare Ezek 38–39, where Gog is a ruler “of the land of Magog”; the meaning of the names is uncertain. Here both stand for the hostile nations.
Compare 2 Kgs 1:10–12; Ezek 38:22. Later manuscripts read “from God out of heaven.”
Compare Dan 7:10; 12:1.
The lake of fire: Westcott and Hort print these words at the end of the verse; some manuscripts omit them.

verses.text: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had vanished, and the sea is no more.{a}
I saw the holy city too—a new Jerusalem—descending from God out of heaven, adorned like a bride made ready for her husband.{b}

A loud voice from the throne declared:
“Look! God’s tent is among human beings.
He will pitch it among them,
and they will be his peoples,
with God himself present among them as their God.{c}
Then the one seated on the throne declared, “Look, I make everything new!” And he said, “Write this down, because these words are faithful and true.”{e}
Then he said to me, “They have come to pass! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end. To the thirsty one I will give as a gift out of the spring of life-giving water.{f}
Whoever conquers will have this as an inheritance; I will be his God, and he will be my son.{g}

But for the cowards, the unbelieving, the vile, murderers, fornicators, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars: the lake that blazes with fire and sulfur will be their portion—this is the second death.”{h}

And there approached me one of those seven angels, those having the seven bowls that were filled with the final seven plagues; he spoke with me and said, “Come here; I will point out to you the bride, the Lamb’s wife.”
And in the Spirit he carried me off to a mountain great and high, and he displayed to me the holy city Jerusalem as it came down out of heaven from God,{i}
shining with the glory of God. Its radiance was like a rare jewel, like jasper, crystal clear.{j}
It had a wall, great and high; it had twelve gates, and over the gates twelve angels, and engraved names, which are those of the twelve tribes of Israel’s sons.{k}
There were three gates facing east, three facing north, three facing south, and three facing west.
The city’s wall rested on twelve foundations, and written on them were twelve names: those of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
The one speaking with me had a golden measuring rod, in order to measure the city, along with its gates and its wall.{l}
The city lies foursquare, with its length equal to its width. With the rod he measured the city: about 1,400 miles. Its length, width, and height are identical.{m}
Its wall he also measured, 216 feet, using a human unit of measure, which was the angel’s.{n}
Its wall was constructed of jasper, and the city itself was pure gold, resembling clear glass.
The foundations of the city’s wall were adorned with all kinds of precious stones: the first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, chalcedony; the fourth, emerald;{o}
the fifth sardonyx, the sixth carnelian, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase, the eleventh jacinth, the twelfth amethyst.{p}
And twelve pearls were the twelve gates—every gate fashioned from one single pearl. The city’s broad street was pure gold, transparent as glass.{q}
No temple did I see in it, for the Lord God, the Almighty, is its temple, and so is the Lamb.{r}
The city requires neither sun nor moon to shine upon it, since God’s glory gave it light, and it has the Lamb as its lamp.{s}
The nations will walk by means of its light, and the kings of the earth carry their glory into it.{t}
Its gates will not be closed by day—and night will not exist there.{u}
They will carry the glory and the honor of the nations into it.
Nothing profane will ever enter it, nor anyone who commits abomination and falsehood, only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s book of life.{v}

notes.text: Compare Isa 52:1; 61:10.
Lev 26:11–12; Ezek 37:27; Zech 2:10–11. *Dwelling*: literally “tent.” *Peoples*: so Westcott and Hort; many manuscripts read “people.” Some manuscripts add “as their God” at the end.
Compare Isa 43:19.
Isa 55:1. *They are accomplished*: literally “they have come to be.” *Alpha … Omega*: see the note on 1:8.
Echoing Ps 89:26–27 and 2 Sam 7:14.
The faithless: or “the unbelieving.” Later manuscripts add “and sinners” after “cowards.”
Compare Ezek 40:2.
Compare Isa 60:1–2, 19.
Compare Ezek 48:30–35.
Compare Ezek 40:3–5.

About 1,400 miles: Greek “12,000 stadia,” about 2,200 km; a stadion was about 607 feet (185 m). The number is symbolic (12 × 1,000). The city is a cube, like the inner sanctuary of Solomon’s temple (1 Kgs 6:20).

216 feet: Greek “144 cubits,” about 65 m; a cubit was about 18 inches (45 cm). The figure (12 × 12) may refer to the wall’s height or its thickness. *A human unit of measure, which was the angel’s*: literally “a measure of a man, which is of an angel.”

The identification of several of these stones with their modern namesakes is uncertain. Compare the stones of the high priest’s breastpiece (Exod 28:17–20) and of Ezek 28:13. *Sapphire*: probably lapis lazuli.
Carnelian: Greek *sardion*; see the note on 4:3. *Chrysolite*: literally “gold stone,” perhaps a yellow topaz. *Topaz*: perhaps peridot. *Jacinth*: Greek *hyakinthos*, a blue or violet stone.
Compare Isa 54:11–12.
The Lord God, the Almighty: see the note on 1:8.
Isa 60:3, 5, 11. Later manuscripts read “the nations of those who are saved.”
Isa 52:1. *Anyone who commits*: Westcott and Hort bracket the article.

verses.text: Then he showed me a river of water that gives life, as clear as crystal, issuing from the throne belonging to God and to the Lamb{a}
