midway along the city’s broad street; and on this bank and that of the river stood a tree of life, which yields twelve harvests, rendering its fruit month by month. The tree’s leaves serve to heal the nations.{b}
No accursed thing will exist any longer. In the city will stand the throne of God and the Lamb, and his slaves will worship him;{c}
they will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads.{d}
And night will exist no longer; nor will they need the light of a lamp or of the sun, for the Lord God will cast his light on them; and they will rule as kings for ever and ever.{e}
And the angel said to me, “These words are faithful and true. The Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, commissioned his angel to show his slaves the things that must soon take place.”{f}
“Look, I am on my way soon! Blessed is whoever heeds the prophetic words of this book.”
I, John, am the one who heard these things and saw them. After I had heard and seen, I prostrated myself in homage at the angel’s feet—the angel who was pointing these things out to me.
But he said to me, “Do not do that! I am a slave together with you, with your brothers the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God.”{g}
And he told me, “Do not seal up the words of this book’s prophecy, for the time is near.{h}
Let the one who does wrong go on doing wrong, and let the one who is filthy go on being filthy; let the righteous go on practicing righteousness, and let the holy go on being made holy.”{i}
“Look, I am on my way soon, and my reward is with me, to give to each one as his work deserves.{j}
I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.”
Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that the tree of life will be theirs by right, and they may enter the city through its gates.{k}
Outside are the dogs, the sorcerers, the sexually immoral, the murderers, the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.{l}
“I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify these things to you about the churches. I am the descendant of David and the root from which he sprang, the bright star of the morning.”{m}
The Spirit and the bride are saying, “Come!” And whoever hears should also say, “Come!” Whoever is thirsty should come; whoever wishes should receive the water of life as a gift.{n}
I give this warning to everyone who hears the words of this book’s prophecy: should anyone add to them, God will lay on him the plagues described in this book;{o}
and if anyone cuts anything from the words of the book containing this prophecy, God will cut off his allotment, whether in the tree of life or in the holy city—things written about in this book.{p}
The one who gives these testimonies says, “Certainly, I am on my way soon.” Amen! Come, Lord Jesus!{q}
The grace of the Lord Jesus be with the saints.{r}

notes.text: Tree of life: Gen 2:9; compare Ezek 47:12. *Down the middle of the city’s street*: these words may instead go with what follows: “Between the street and the river, on either side, stood the tree of life.” *Tree*: the Greek may be collective, “trees.”
Compare Zech 14:11.
Compare Ps 17:15; Exod 33:20.
Isa 60:19; Dan 7:18, 27. *Give them light*: Westcott and Hort bracket the Greek preposition “upon.”
The God of the spirits of the prophets: compare Num 16:22; 27:16. Later manuscripts read “the God of the holy prophets.”
Brothers: Greek *adelphoi*, which includes sisters.
Contrast Dan 12:4, 9.
Compare Dan 12:10.
Who wash their robes: so Westcott and Hort, with Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus; later manuscripts read “who do his commandments.”
Dogs: a term of contempt for the impure; compare Deut 23:18; Phil 3:2.
Isa 11:1, 10; Num 24:17. *To you*: the Greek is plural.
Compare Deut 4:2; 12:32.

Tree of life: so Westcott and Hort and the early Greek manuscripts. The King James Version’s “book of life” goes back to Erasmus, whose single Greek manuscript lacked the last verses of the book; he translated them from the Latin Vulgate, whose text in many copies reads *libro*, “book,” for *ligno*, “tree.”
Quickly: Greek *tachy*, also “soon,” as in 22:7, 12.

Lord Jesus: Westcott and Hort bracket “Christ” after “Jesus.” *With the saints*: so Westcott and Hort, with Sinaiticus; Alexandrinus reads “with all,” and later manuscripts “with you all” or “with all the saints.” Later manuscripts add “Amen.”
